root_cause.text: In sched_ext, callers could be preempted after scx_claim_exit() set scx_sched->exit_kind but before queueing the helper kthread work, creating a non-atomic exit path where error handling was already disabled and teardown/bypass might never be started.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message and added comment state that once scx_claim_exit() claims exit_kind, “scx_error() can no longer trigger,” so if the task is “preempted between claiming exit and kicking the helper work,” the work “is never queued,” “bypass mode never activates,” and “the whole system can wedge”; the patch fixes this by adding preemption guards in scx_disable() and scx_vexit() and lockdep_assert_preemption_disabled() in scx_claim_exit().

agent_logs.evidence_points: The commit message and added comment state that once scx_claim_exit() claims exit_kind, “scx_error() can no longer trigger,” so if the task is “preempted between claiming exit and kicking the helper work,” the work “is never queued,” “bypass mode never activates,” and “the whole system can wedge”; the patch fixes this by adding preemption guards in scx_disable() and scx_vexit() and lockdep_assert_preemption_disabled() in scx_claim_exit().

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a preemption-disabled assertion to scx_claim_exit() to enforce its required calling context and catch conditions that could wedge the system during scheduler exit.
intent_record.what: A descriptive comment was added above scx_claim_exit(), and a new lockdep_assert_preemption_disabled() statement was inserted at the start of the function before the atomic_try_cmpxchg() on sch->exit_kind.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the new assertion checks in lockdep/debug builds that preemption is disabled when scx_claim_exit() is called, enforcing the requirement that exit claiming and helper work kick happen without the current task being preempted; this helps catch incorrect call contexts that could otherwise leave helper work untriggered and wedge the system.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a preemption guard in scx_disable() to protect exit claiming and disable-work queueing from preemption-related races.
intent_record.what: A single statement, guard(preempt)();, was added inside the if (sch) block in scx_disable() immediately before calling scx_claim_exit(sch, kind) and kthread_queue_work(sch->helper, &sch->disable_work).
intent_record.how: At runtime, this introduces a preemption guard for the critical section that operates on the scheduler object after it is obtained under RCU, preventing the current task from being preempted while claiming exit and queueing the disable work. This helps ensure those operations execute in a protected context and avoids races or invalid state transitions caused by preemption.

intent_record.intent_summary: Disable preemption at the start of `scx_vexit()` to protect the exit-claim critical section from preemption-related races.
intent_record.what: A new `guard(preempt)();` statement was inserted at the start of `scx_vexit()` immediately after loading `sch->exit_info` and before the call to `scx_claim_exit(sch, kind)`.
intent_record.how: This makes the function execute within a preemption-disabled guard scope, preventing the current task from being preempted while entering the scheduler exit path and attempting to claim exit state, which helps avoid races or inconsistent state during that critical section.

grouping_result.intent: Disable preemption at the start of `scx_vexit()` to protect the exit-claim critical section from preemption-related races.

consistency_review.core_intent: Harden the scheduler-exit/disable path against preemption-related races by requiring or enforcing non-preemptible execution around exit claiming and related critical sections.

relevance_review.reason: The changes directly target the root cause: a preemption window between scx_claim_exit() setting exit_kind and queueing the helper work. Adding preemption-disabled assertions and guards around scx_claim_exit(), scx_disable(), and scx_vexit() enforces atomic, non-preemptible execution of the scheduler exit path.

candidates.rationale: This claims exit and sets exit_kind without any preemption protection in the shown caller, creating the vulnerable window where the task can be preempted after error handling is disabled but before teardown/bypass work is queued.

This is the follow-up action that must happen immediately after exit is claimed; because it was not protected as part of an atomic non-preemptible critical section with the prior claim, preemption before this statement could leave exit processing unstarted.

This invokes the exit-claim path in scx_vexit() without the preemption-disabled context later required by the fix, exposing the same race between claiming exit and proceeding with the rest of exit handling.

This is the statement inside scx_claim_exit() that actually flips exit_kind atomically, but by itself does not make the larger exit path atomic against preemption; once this succeeds, callers can be preempted before queueing helper work.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement claims exit and sets the scheduler's exit state before helper work is queued. The root cause is the non-atomic window after exit is claimed but before teardown/bypass work is started, and this line is the point where that vulnerable state begins in scx_disable().

This statement enters the same exit-claim path from scx_vexit() without the preemption-disabled protection required by the fix. It exposes the same race where exit has been claimed but subsequent exit handling may be interrupted before completion.

Author: Tejun Heo <tj@kernel.org>
Date:   Tue Nov 11 09:18:07 2025 -1000

    sched_ext: Simplify breather mechanism with scx_aborting flag
    
    The breather mechanism was introduced in 62dcbab8b0ef ("sched_ext: Avoid
    live-locking bypass mode switching") and e32c260195e6 ("sched_ext: Enable the
    ops breather and eject BPF scheduler on softlockup") to prevent live-locks by
    injecting delays when CPUs are trapped in dispatch paths.
bic_trace_step.reason:
The snippet is sufficient because it shows the full exit-claim helper and both call sites that initiate disable/exit. The vulnerable construct is present in `scx_claim_exit()`:

- `if (!atomic_try_cmpxchg(&sch->exit_kind, &none, kind)) return false;`
- then only afterwards: `WRITE_ONCE(scx_aborting, true);`

This matches the root cause: exit is claimed first by setting `sch->exit_kind`, but the mechanism that starts the abort/breather path is enabled only in a separate later step. A caller can be preempted after `exit_kind` is set and before `scx_aborting` is set, creating a non-atomic exit transition.

The same helper is then used by the paths which queue teardown work later:

- in `scx_disable()`: `scx_claim_exit(sch, kind); kthread_queue_work(sch->helper, &sch->disable_work);`
- in `scx_vexit()`: `if (!scx_claim_exit(sch, kind)) return; ...`

So there is still a window where `exit_kind` has already been claimed but the abort handling / breather enablement has not yet been activated, and queueing of helper work happens even later. That is exactly the non-atomic exit-path issue described.

The fix is not present because the code does not make claiming exit and initiating abort/teardown indivisible; instead it performs them as separate operations in sequence. Therefore `has_bug=true` and `is_fixed=false`.

In `scx_ops_exit_kind()`, the function first claims the exit by atomically setting `scx_exit_kind` from `SCX_EXIT_NONE` to the requested kind via `if (!atomic_try_cmpxchg(&scx_exit_kind, &none, kind)) return;`, and then later queues the async teardown with `irq_work_queue(&scx_ops_error_irq_work);`.
